- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive or trending upward; reduce initial forecast peaks if sentiment is weak or turning negative.
- Underestimate sharp downward moves after spikes; model should anticipate mean reversion in sentiment-neutral or negative sentiment periods.
- Avoid over-optimistic late-period forecasts (especially >20d horizon) when sentiment is declining or mixed; cap upward momentum if sentiment drops below 0.3.
- Correct for lagged price drops: if true outcome shows a sharp decline after a forecast peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 days if sentiment remains flat or negative.
- When sentiment is consistently above 0.5, model should not over-forecast price increases beyond 10–15% above recent high; apply downward bias if sentiment is >0.7 and price is rising.
- If sentiment is negative or near-zero, reduce forecast by 3–5% for each day of negative sentiment history, especially in the first 7–10 days of forecast horizon.
- Avoid forecasting price spikes after recent high sentiment; if sentiment drops below 0.3 after a peak, reduce forecast by 10–20% for the next 5–7 days.
